analysis.title: The Trump Put Delivers: Jensen Is Back, Nasdaq Futures Halted... And Goldman's Privorotsky Asks Whether To Sell The Squeeze
key_insights: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO effective immediately, about 11 hours after a Trump Truth Social post. The board cited input from senior levels of the US government. NVDA rose as much as 30% premarket, S&P futures were up 4.6% at highs and Nasdaq futures were halted.

Goldman equity analysts retain a Buy on Nvidia and expect the multiple to re-rate. They say DOJ export-control and SEC disclosure investigations remain an overhang until resolved or more disclosure is provided.

Privorotsky had flagged the Trump put earlier Monday. He said the acute drivers of last week's selloff were Nvidia export restrictions, remote compute access, TSMC licensing uncertainty and an AI backdrop with growth deceleration and accounting questions.

A rhetorical pivot is not regulatory relief. Bessent still defends the remote access restrictions, investigations stay active, and the real test is whether licenses are granted for offshore data centers.

Positioning was washed out. GS PB data show fundamental L/S net leverage at the 1st percentile over one year, beta-adjusted net at a 5-year low, and the largest weekly shorting since April 2025. This set up a bear market rally.

Sentiment was extreme into the weekend. VIX touched about 40, CNN Fear & Greed was near 10, put/call near the 95th percentile, and the VIX curve was at its steepest inversion since April 2025. GS Panic Index hit a record 9.8.

Privorotsky argues the Fed is mispriced. Fedspeak is the most hawkish since 2023 while markets price a growth shock, commodities have collapsed, inflation expectations are near yearly lows, real rates are too high and financial conditions have tightened materially.
The analog is Nov/Dec 2018. Privorotsky says credit is the tell: if Nvidia rallies but neocloud spreads stay under pressure, it is likely just short covering.

The author leans skeptical on the squeeze. Suggested approach is to let it breathe through Thanksgiving and sell if neocloud spreads do not follow Nvidia. Thin holiday liquidity could amplify the move.
Week ahead catalysts: flash PMIs Monday, Dell earnings Tuesday, and Beige Book plus core PCE Wednesday, ahead of payrolls, the December FOMC and November CPI.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman keeps Buy after Huang's reinstatement and expects a re-rating. DOJ and SEC investigations remain an overhang.

sector_views.rationale: AI infrastructure depends on external capital as its cost rises. The reinstatement does not solve financing or oversupply, and junk bonds had their biggest blowout of 2026.

earnings_insights: Dell reports earnings Tuesday. No estimates are given in the report.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since early 2023, up from about -5 at the start of the year, versus the 19.2 peak in June 2022. This shows very hawkish Fed rhetoric.
Seen as the marquee inflation release ahead of payrolls, the December FOMC and November CPI.
Tightening is material and the Fed has not acknowledged it, which is a risk to multiples.

trade_ideas.description: Let the squeeze breathe through Thanksgiving, then sell the rally if neocloud credit spreads do not follow Nvidia higher
trade_ideas.rationale: Credit is the tell, and a rehired CEO does not fix financing or oversupply.
trade_ideas.risk: Short covering and thin liquidity could extend the squeeze.

risk_factors: The DOJ and SEC investigations into Nvidia remain active.
Offshore data center licenses have not been granted.
Fed over-tightening and a hawkish FOMC, with Waller pitching 50bp hikes.
Neocloud and AI debt stress, with Gartner expecting over 80% of neoclouds to fold.
Short-covering rally may fade as in 2018.
charts_described: Bloomberg Economics Fedspeak sentiment index closed at 14.1, roughly the highest since early 2023 and up from about -5 at the start of the year, with a 19.2 peak in June 2022 (levels read off the chart, approximate).
vol_and_positioning: VIX touched about 40 into the weekend, with genuine left tail stress.
GS Panic Index hit a record 9.8 after the fifth-biggest VIX spike on record.
Historically VIX closes above 35 have often preceded positive equity reversals over following weeks. Privorotsky calls the sample small and not a forecast.
Fundamental L/S gross leverage was 204.8% (13th percentile) and net 42.3% (1st percentile 1-year).
CFTC leveraged funds were reportedly net short Nasdaq futures.
Put/call ratios were near the 95th percentile and the VIX curve was at its steepest inversion since April 2025.
Thanksgiving thin liquidity could amplify the squeeze.
geopolitical: Trump publicly pushed for Huang's reinstatement and the Attorney General said the government has no evidence of unlawful conduct.
The US BIS regime squeezes China on chips, remote compute and overseas foundries.
The DOJ is investigating possible export control violations tied to shipments to jurisdictions including Singapore.
Over the weekend China lowered margin requirements, Korea eased buyback curbs and Taiwan tightened short-selling rules.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Tony Pasquariello was mapping signposts for a tactical bottom.
Morgan Stanley's Savone cited hedge fund nets closing in on COVID lows.
Goldman's top derivs trader used the Nov/Dec 2018 analog last week.

tension_points.bull_case: Extreme positioning, elevated vol, the Nvidia pivot and a visible Trump put create a compelling tactical setup. VIX closes above 35 have often preceded rebounds.
tension_points.bear_case: A rehired CEO does not grant licenses, lower real rates or fix AI financing. Fed hawkishness and neocloud credit stress persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia rallies while neocloud spreads remain under pressure, which would signal only short covering.

theme_stances.key_argument: The rally is a tactical positioning squeeze and credit spreads in neoclouds will show whether it is a genuine recovery.
Markets price a growth shock while Fed rhetoric is hawkish, so real rates look too high.
theme_stances.evidence: I will continue my overtures about the mispricing of the Fed.
